title: Pricing a new product before the first sale
target: How to set a new product's first price in Supermarket Simulator before it sells: market cost, pricing screen margin, quick picks, dynamic goods and offers.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A product you can order at your shop's current level
The product's market cost visible while you order
A shelf slot or display slot that can take the first delivery
Enough cash for the first order

steps.do: Start from the buying list and confirm the product is there before you plan a price around it.
steps.because: what can be bought is kept as sales items with a kind of sale of its own, so the list is the catalogue the shop is working from (SalesItem, SalesType)

steps.do: Check the shop level the product asks for, because a price is no use on a product you cannot order yet.
steps.because: a product can carry a required store level before it can be ordered (RequiredStoreLevel)

steps.do: Read the market's cost for that product on the day you order, rather than the price you remember paying.
steps.because: the market keeps a product cost and a displayed price as separate values, so the two can move apart (LocalMarketProductCost, LocalMarketProductPriceDisplay)

steps.do: Set the first price on the pricing screen, not by copying the cost onto a shelf tag.
steps.because: prices are set on a canvas of their own through a price manager and evaluated by a manager of their own (SettingPriceCanvas, PriceManager, PriceEvaluationManager)

steps.do: Use the margin the screen computes as the test of the number you typed.
steps.because: the screen computes the margins it needs through a delegate of its own (ComputeRequiredMarginsDelegate)

steps.do: Treat a quick pick as a shortcut to a price you have already decided, not as the decision itself.
steps.because: a price can be picked quickly through quick-pick buttons, a group, a mode and their own data (PriceQuickPickButton, PriceQuickPickGroup, PriceQuickPickMode, PriceQuickPickSO)

steps.do: Check whether the product prices itself before you fix a margin on it.
steps.because: there is a kind of product whose price is dynamic rather than fixed (DynamicPriceProduct)

steps.do: Keep a wholesale offer and a discount out of the shelf price, and count each where it belongs.
steps.because: offers run through their own manager, carry a kind and a time limit and are accepted rather than applied automatically, while discounts have their own manager and rate (WholeSaleManager, OfferType, offertime, CanAcceptOffer, DiscountManager, discountRate)

steps.do: Before the first box is shelved, check the slot that will hold it rather than only the shelf's total space.
steps.because: a shelf is made of rack slots and display slots with their own records, and a display slot can carry a condition on what may be placed in it (RackSlot, DisplaySlot, IDisplaySlotProductPlacementCondition)

steps.do: Let the first day's own record tell you whether the price worked before you change it again.
steps.because: the game keeps a daily record with a manager and a screen of its own, and a price change is evaluated and raises a notification (dailyProfit, DailyStatisticsData, DailyStatisticsManager, DailyStatisticsScreen, PriceEvaluationManager, PriceChangeNotification)

commonMistakes: Pricing the new product from the cost of the last one instead of its own market cost.
Copying the market cost onto the shelf and leaving no margin.
Using a quick pick without checking the margin it leaves.
Treating a wholesale offer or a discount as if it were the shelf price.
Shelving the first delivery before checking that a slot can take it.
Reading the till total instead of the day's own record when judging the first price.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
